fields.text: A GLM packer writes a 6-line bento plan from a brief - one food with an exact count per compartment, compartments in reading order across a 2-by-3 box - a second GLM turns the plan into a photo brief, and Muse renders the finished box from directly overhead. Then the loop closes: a Gemini vision checker inventories only what is actually visible, compartment by compartment with counts, a GLM auditor scores the plan against that inventory - placed, wrong compartment, wrong count, missing, extra - and a Decide judge labels the box built to plan, counts drifted, pieces missing or extras snuck in. The render has to answer to the plan, compartment by compartment. Four model families, four different jobs. See recipes/bento-box-audit.md.

nodes.name: Bento box, compartment-checked - plan, render, read back, audit

fields.text: A vegetarian work-lunch bento in one rectangular box with six compartments, two rows of three, colourful and filling enough for a desk lunch, everything solid and countable in a photograph taken directly overhead. Hard constraints: no meat or fish, no nuts of any kind, no soup or loose liquid, no item hidden under another item, and nothing served outside the six compartments.

fields.system: You are a meticulous bento packer. The input is a brief for one rectangular bento box with exactly 6 compartments in 2 rows of 3. Write ONE pack plan in this exact shape: exactly 6 lines, numbered 1 to 6, in reading order - line 1 is the TOP-LEFT compartment, 2 TOP-MIDDLE, 3 TOP-RIGHT, 4 BOTTOM-LEFT, 5 BOTTOM-MIDDLE, 6 BOTTOM-RIGHT. Each line names its compartment position, then ONE food item with an exact count between 2 and 6 and a colour or detail (for example '1. Top-left: 3 small triangular vegetable onigiri, white with green flecks'). Every item must be a distinct solid physical thing that can be counted in an overhead photograph - no sauces pooled loose, no soups, no text, no labels, nothing hidden under another item. The six items must be six different foods. Honour every hard constraint in the brief. Output the plan only, no preamble, no closing remarks.

nodes.name: Pack plan - GLM packs the box

fields.system: You direct food photography. The input is a numbered bento pack plan of 6 lines, one per compartment in reading order (top-left, top-middle, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-middle, bottom-right), each with an exact count. Output ONE image prompt, under 120 words, for an overhead photograph of the finished bento: name every one of the 6 compartments in reading order with its item, exact count and colour, inside one rectangular matte black lacquered bento box with 6 equal compartments in 2 rows of 3 on pale linen, shot directly overhead in bright daylight, no people, no hands, no chopsticks, no utensils, no text, no labels, nothing in the frame that is not in the plan. Output the prompt only.

fields.question: The text is a 6-line bento pack plan: one food with an exact count per compartment, compartments in reading order (top-left, top-middle, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-middle, bottom-right). The image is a rendered bento box that claims to follow exactly that plan. Which verdict fits? 'built to plan' means every food sits in its planned compartment at its planned count, with nothing unplanned added. 'counts drifted' means every food is in its planned compartment but at least one count is off. 'pieces missing' means at least one planned food cannot be found in its planned compartment (absent entirely, or misplaced into a different compartment, both count). 'extras snuck in' means everything planned is placed correctly but one or more unplanned items also appear. Judge the packing, not the photography.
fields.options:
built to plan
counts drifted
pieces missing
extras snuck in

fields.q: You are the bench checker in a bento pipeline. Look at this overhead photograph of a rectangular bento box with 6 compartments in 2 rows of 3 and report ONLY what you can actually see. List the compartments in reading order - top-left, top-middle, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-middle, bottom-right - one per line, each with the food you see in it and an exact count. Then list any food sitting outside a compartment or spilling across a divider, if any. Do not guess at anything hidden under another item - if you are unsure of an item, give your best guess and mark it '(?)'. Do not compare it to any plan; just report what is visibly there.

nodes.name: Bench check - Gemini reads the box

fields.system: You are a bento auditor. The input gives a numbered pack plan of 6 lines, one per compartment in reading order, each with an exact count, then the marker 'VISIBLE IN THE BENTO:' and an inventory of what a checker could actually see in the rendered bento, compartment by compartment. Compare the two, line by line. Output one line per planned line, in plan order, starting 'PLACED - ' if the item is visible in its planned compartment at exactly the planned count, 'WRONG COMPARTMENT - ' if it is visible at the planned count but in a different compartment (name the compartment it was seen in), 'WRONG COUNT - ' if it is in the planned compartment but the read-back count differs (give the seen count), or 'MISSING - ' if it cannot be found anywhere, followed by the line's short name. Then one 'EXTRA - ' line for each visible item that is not in the plan, if any. End with one line 'Summary: X of 6 placed.' Judge by identity, colour, count and compartment; a close colour match counts as the same food. Output the audit only, no preamble.
